summary: Priority-shift causing pool reservation tunneling and mid-day GPU starvation for Nova Finance (dedicated)
description:
Issue summary:
Midday on 2025-08-19 Nova Finance (dedicated pool) experienced a sudden p50/p99 throughput collapse for short-burst chat routes. Requests queued; autoscaler did not attach additional GPU capacity in time. Customers saw elevated 429s and 504s for ~15 minutes before partial recovery via manual mitigation.

Impact:
- Customer-facing: 20% of requests returned errors or timeouts during the event window; bulk of traffic served by pinned slot pool.
- Business: Nova Finance is a production dedicated customer with SLA commitments.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: pool-id fc-9a2b (Nova Finance reserved)
- Region: us-west (primary)
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Run sustained burst of many short chat streams that multiplex connections (100-200 concurrent short streams) to routes pinned to the reserved pool.
2) Trigger a priority-shift (customer route marked high-priority via routing override) while snapshotter jobs run background checkpoint writes.
3) Observe allocator logs: slot reservations increase but GPU attach latency and IO stalls occur; autoscaler backoff engages.

Notes: Repro requires heavy short-stream fanout + concurrent background snapshot writes (observed in Nova's production schedule).
observed_logs_and_metrics:
- allocator: repeated "attach_timeout" entries at 2025-08-19T14:03:12Z -> 14:10:23Z.
- autoscaler: surge then backoff entries; decision log shows "fragmentation_detected" and "prefetch_pressure" flags.
- snapshotter: elevated NVMe write latency spikes coincident with the event (avg write latency 12x baseline).
- serving-runtime: p99 latency increased from 180ms to 2.4s; token throughput fell 60% for pinned pool.
- Console traces: Queue length for customer routes grew from 5->120.
- No obvious driver/kernel crashes; GPU utilization on attached devices was moderate (35-60%) but many pending attach operations present.
temporary_mitigations:
- Applied routing override to shift some non-critical routes to hosted fallback model variants for 25 minutes (reduced load on reserved pool).
- Manually triggered allocator drain -> reattach cycle on a subset of nodes which recovered stalled attach operations.
- Request to Nova: reschedule snapshotter heavy jobs outside peak window as immediate customer mitigation.
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis: Priority shift created a tunnel effect where high-priority reservation requests repeatedly attempted to carve available fractional GPU capacity while background snapshotter IO caused NVMe latency spikes; this increased attach latency and caused autoscaler to misclassify capacity as unavailable (fragmented slots), triggering cooldown/backoff.
Evidence: Correlated NVMe write latency bursts and allocator attach_timeout spikes. Autoscaler logs include rule matches referencing "fragmentation_detected" after repeated failed attach attempts.
Counter-evidence: Some GPUs attached fine for long-running streams but short-burst streams experienced serialization due to slot fragmentation.
Partial findings:
- Identified two nodes in the reserved pool with snapshotter heavy IO during the window.
- Found allocator code path that treats successive attach failures from the same host as a signal to reduce attach rate for that AZ for a cooldown window (this amplified the recovery delay).
- No customer-side library or SDK change at time of event; traffic profile matched historical baselines but with higher short-stream fanout due to scheduled runbook.

Logs & links:
- Allocator decision trace: https://logs.redwood.local/alloc/trace/fc-9a2b/2025-08-19
- Autoscaler decision dump: https://logs.redwood.local/autoscale/dumps/2025-08-19/err-2025-08-19-14
- NVMe metrics dashboard: https://console.redwood.local/dashboards/nvme/write-latency?pool=fc-9a2b
next_steps:
- Short term: Patch allocator to avoid aggressive cooldown when attach failures are correlated with IO spikes (hotfix branch created: autoscaler PR #1423). Coordinate with infra to throttle snapshotter writes for Nova's pool for next 48 hours.
- Mid term: Add autoscaler rule to consider NVMe health signals and not treat attach failures alone as capacity exhaustion.
- Long term: Improve slot defragmentation heuristics and add a dedicated IO-schedule advisory in Console for Dedicated customers.
- Follow up: Run a controlled load test with snapshotter background IO and short-stream fanout to validate fixes.
Timeline: aim to deploy hotfix to staging 2025-08-20 and to prod canary 2025-08-21 if tests pass.
customer_communication:
Support sent initial acknowledgement 2025-08-19T14:07Z; informed customer we were investigating and applied routing mitigation. Follow-up call scheduled 2025-08-20 09:00 PT with Nova SRE and Red team. Customer requested post-incident report and pledge to implement IO scheduling best-practice guidance.
Status communicated: In Progress. Expected follow-up: Hotfix deployment and advisory within 48 hours.
resolution: Triage ongoing; manual mitigations restored partial capacity and a hotfix branch exists. Final root cause and permanent remediation pending verification in staging.
